_source.frame: Spell keys unlock or normalize wizard magic a plane suppresses (most keys add 1 to initiative/casting time — see law:planar-conditions:general:school-alteration-legend). Power keys are deity-granted tokens restoring priest sphere access away from the power's home turf (the M4 frame: law:planar-priest:*). Named physical keys as ITEMS are Mimir's lane (keyed_to edges); the law of what unlocks what, per plane, lives here.

acheron.spell_keys: Sets of words, motions, and substances rigid in form yet empty of meaning; the ritual must be exact and the form held precisely. Battle-mage tradition names them: a 'gray key' unlocks invisibility, a 'blood key' magic missile, the 'lesser fire key' burning hands, the 'great fire key' every elemental fire spell, a 'swords key' enchanted weapon. No spell keys exist for any form of wild magic.
acheron.power_keys: Rare outside the armies: orc/goblin/hobgoblin officers carry keys for the spheres of Combat, Guardian, Healing, Necromancy, Protection, and War — shaped as florid arcane marching orders or commissions, often time-limited (expiry sometimes written on the key in the baatezu tongue), and sellable for ~1,000 gp+ (owning a STOLEN key is a crime: huge fine and banishment). Lei Kung's keys are absorbed lightning/thunder released a little per spell, transferred only by catching the slain holder's dying breath in a vial; Laduguer's are items forged by the caster, blessed by a duergar priest, functioning only for their maker.

arcadia.spell_keys: Symbolic of the plane and the school — always a piece of the plane, bounded by what the caster wants of it. Divination: clear Arcadian spring water in a rectangular container; illusion: the same water muddied with riverbank mud; elemental: the element itself taken from natural surroundings, bounded by an ordinary shape; conjuration: something of the plane that would tempt the desired creature.
arcadia.power_keys: More strictly regulated than anywhere but Mechanus; granted only where they'll do the most good, and most lose their power weekly. Desert powers (Ra, Osiris, Isis, Horus): silver or petrified-wood ankhs and scarabs. Dwarven powers (Clangeddin, Reorx): small anvils, golden battle axes, mithral hammers. Meriadar: a decorated silver bowl — components go in the bowl, raised overhead. Other powers' keys tie to their worship.

baator.spell_keys: Per-layer, multiplying with depth: on Avernus a single simple key — obsidian broken off the River of Blood's banks — unlocks any spell; each layer down needs progressively more keys (3 on Dis, 9, 27, 81...) until on Nessus nearly every spell wants its own. Stability also varies: layers 1-3 keys almost never change, 4-6 shift roughly every century, 7-9 switch without apparent rhyme (though with some pattern).
baator.power_keys: Granted by the gods of the Nine Layers for advantage — and FALSE keys are endemic (handed to rival powers' priests; nonfunctional, embarrassing, or deadly; a knowing eye can spot something slightly askew). A true key usually resembles the granting deity's unholy symbol or is carved from petitioner bone/spirit; it works best in the deity's realm, normally across the power's layer, rarely plane-wide. Common spheres: Charm, Combat, Necromantic, Law, Thought, War, Wards.

mechanus.spell_keys: Two kinds. (1) Cog-twelfths: each twelfth of a cog bears a school's sigil and color (all schools including the four elemental, excluding necromancy); joined into a whole cog the caster may absorb it — casting ANY spell at will within Mechanus thereafter, but at half efficiency outside; the key is permanent (a cog tattoo), dissolves on death, and excision kills the bearer. (2) The necromantic key: a piece of a modron plus a muttered formula directed at Shang-ti's realm (kept dark); it also waives the school's flesh/hit-point component price.
mechanus.power_keys: Always little cogs, by every power's convention. Each is good for exactly one day; at day's end the key — and whoever carries it — returns to the granting power's realm, where the power or a proxy decides renewal (the rightful owner is sent back where he was taken from; a thief ends the day facing the power). This makes Mechanus one of the safest planes to hold a power key.

mount-celestia.spell_keys: All metal, composition scaling with spell level, the SHAPE declaring the school: hearts (necromancy), stars (conjuration), bowls (divination), circles (abjuration), cups (enchantment), wands (alteration), dust or filings (illusion), blades or spikes (invocation/evocation). The channel must be noble metal at its purest — flawless gold, untarnished silver — and the key's purity gates the casting alongside the caster's own (the alignment ladder in law:planar-conditions:mount-celestia).
mount-celestia.power_keys: Frequently granted, strictly regulated: nonchaotic, nonevil characters can earn them, and all keys rotate every 30, 60, or 90 days, capping the value of stolen ones. Sun gods: bright, glittering, sometimes blinding tokens. Brihaspati: simple scrolls. Dwarven gods: metal tools — hammers, anvils. Halfling powers: homely comforts (pipe smoke, a slow-cooked meal, a decanted wine). Bahamut: golden treasure-shaped keys, granted to any dragon who asks.

the-abyss.spell_keys: Bribes to the lords and powers to let the spell pass — blood or money, usually not the caster's. Necromancy: a death. Elemental: fouling or destroying a pure substance. Alteration: mingling the caster's and recipient's blood. Conjuration/summoning: a toll of wealth equal to 100 gp x spell level (gold draws a rutterkin; only gems tempt a succubus or babau; true tanar'ri answer only to magical items). Divination keys are hoarded by the lords — each divination spell has a SPECIFIC key (shattering a mirror, drinking unholy oil, knowing the subject's full true name). False keys abound (casting while beating a gong; drinking boiling oil — 1d8 damage and a Constitution ability check or lose verbal spells 2-16 days); the most dangerous false key uses the subject's written name, and naming a tanar'ri in a spell always draws its attention at double the usual consequences.
the-abyss.power_keys: Vanishingly rare. Abyssal lords' keys are shrunken manes-skull amulets (skin and hair intact) holding a sliver of the lord's own power — working only on the open layers and the granting lord's layers. Abyssal powers' keys mimic their unholy symbols and work outside the power's realm only on a mission furthering that power's ends.

arborea.spell_keys: Ritual offerings to the earth and nature spirits (wine, oat cakes, milk, gold, olive oil, unblemished animals, the mage's own blood), scaling by school and level. Conjuration/summoning: food for the creature (low), a carved image of it (mid), speaking its language (high) — force-conjuring spells need none. Divination: an inanimate offering (low), an animate key such as freed doves or a goat's liver (mid), a treasured possession of the caster's (high). Enchantment/charm: capture the target's attention with a joke or riddle — puns are bad form (low); know the target's name, group names sufficing for group spells (mid); offer something the target desires (high). Necromancy: dark gems (low), a goblet of sap/fresh blood/life-giving liquid (mid), pure life energy (high). Elemental: a gift of the OPPOSITE element, scaling (a bucket of water for burning hands; a small forest fire to balance transmute dust to water).
arborea.power_keys: Handed out with wild abandon and revoked at whim — many last a single trip. Greek gods: emblems of the god's colors, triumphs, or symbols (Hermes' sandals, Athena's owl feather, Ares' bloody spear), hard to hide. The Seldarine: subtle pieces of the natural world (staves sprouting green leaves, ever-blooming flowers, bottled wind released bit by bit, laurel crowns, feather robes, herbal infusions, minerals carved into pipes, blades, chalices).

limbo.spell_keys: Mostly serve to waive Limbo's Intelligence test (some also unlock Inner-Planes summoning). No key ever repeats — not even for the same caster: keys are insight in the moment. Procedure: a successful Spellcraft proficiency roll to recognize what would serve as a key right now, then a Wisdom test to will the components into existence from the chaos-stuff. Two natures: keys of CHANGE (a blown smoke ring, salt dissolving in water — the change itself is the key, cast as it happens, components consumed) suit Alteration, Enchantment/Charm, Illusion/Phantasm; keys of BALANCE (a spinning coin, a dagger poised on a fingertip; stronger keys add risked destruction — an egg or glass sphere balanced on a staff tip) suit Abjuration, Conjuration/Summoning, Invocation/Evocation.
limbo.power_keys: Open-handedly granted: the award IS the test — unfaithful priests lose the key exactly when they need it most, and Limbo's powers sometimes negate one out of sheer caprice. Most-granted spheres: Charm, Creation, Elemental (Fenmarel Mestarine prefers Weather over Elemental).

pandemonium.spell_keys: Wind through rock: flutes, whistles, and jugs carved from Pandemonium's stone, held to catch the plane's wind (water added to a jug changes its pitch). Specific tones, combinations, and sequences serve as individual keys — the more grating and discordant the better, and it must sound louder than the plane's own howl.
pandemonium.power_keys: The reclusive powers here are stingy. What they grant runs to the spheres of Charm (to promote chaos), Guardian (to shield their agents), and Necromantic (to promote evil).

ysgard.spell_keys: The runes, first won by Odin at the Well of Knowledge and passed to the worthy: each school's key is a rune or rune-set, carved onto the spell's material components or spoken aloud if it has none. Per school: abjuration — shield-rune and iron-can't-bite-rune; alteration — change-rune and strength-rune; conjuration — gathering-rune; divination — fortune-rune and lore-rune; enchantment/charm — charm-rune, follow-rune, nith-rune; illusion/phantasm — sight-rune and speech-rune; invocation/evocation — triumph-rune and berserk-rune; necromancy — dead-rune, disease-rune, help-rune, limb-rune; wild magic — chaos-rune; air — shout-rune; earth — strength-rune; fire — quench-rune and spark-rune; water — sea-rune. Runes can also be found carved beneath Yggdrasil's bark near the roots, or at the Well of Mimir (past its giant guardian). A few special spells demand KENNINGS instead — fire wants 'the terror of the birch', battle-magic the 'play of spears'.
ysgard.power_keys: Earned in the deity's eyes — Odin, Thor, Frigga, Loki, and Heimdall grant most, each releasing spells of that power's interest; only Thor's most faithful hold the weather key, never another deity's worshipers. Stolen keys die the moment the power notices — except Loki's: the god of thieves rewards anyone able to steal from him. The other powers grant on whim (usually their symbol or holy object); Combat and Guardian spheres flow most freely, to shield followers from the battle-mad petitioners.

the-beastlands.spell_keys: Natural items — the larger the item, the higher the spell level it empowers. Abjuration: stones and pebbles (elemental aura's key). Alteration: leaves on the wind. Conjuration/summoning: a foodstuff suited to the creature called (hay or oats for a horse, a fresh haunch for a great cat), or a large quantity of the element for a pseudoelemental. Divination: silver ore. Enchantment/charm: rock crystals, quartz, geodes. Illusion/phantasm: feathers (whispering wind's key). Invocation/evocation: branches off lightning-struck trees (the key for wall of fog, stinking cloud, cloudkill). Necromancy: bone of the general creature type to be affected. Elemental: a naturally created instance of the element (smoke from a fire for Air, a bonfire for Fire, and so on).
the-beastlands.power_keys: Rarely issued — the nature powers hold that nature self-corrects; keys come only against dire threats to a realm, the plane, or their Prime worshipers' domain. Stronmaus and the powers of Krynn and Toril are the most likely granters (the giant god's keys take metallic form).
the-beastlands.ocr_note: the description of Stronmaus's key shape is cut at the witnessed page edge ('a metallic ...'); shape detail beyond 'metallic' is unattested here.

bytopia.spell_keys: Hand-crafted items or tools evoking the school being restored — and they MUST be manufactured by Bytopian hands on one of the two layers (a nonnative with carpentry cannot carve his own). Conjuration/summoning keys are rare (the school's restriction resists craftwork). Divination: a spyglass or ear trumpet. The necromancy key is deliberately kept dark by the plane's folk. Wide-ranging elemental spells are restored by mimicking the intended effect (dig a shovel of ground to move earth).
bytopia.power_keys: The gnomish gods are generous to gnomes in need; keys usually last just long enough to escape the trouble at hand, then die. Garl Glittergold: gold or jewelry; Flandal Steelskin: small hammers engraved with flames; virtually every gnomish key grants Major access to the Protection and Elemental spheres. Ilmater: a strong blood-red cord wrapped around the priest's wrist — All, Healing, Protection spheres. Kiri-Jolith (to Knights of Solamnia, especially the Order of the Sword): All, Combat, Healing, Sun spheres for the quest's duration.

elysium.spell_keys: Only nonevil spellcasters find keys that function for them — and little is needed, since the plane barely hampers good casters. A needed key matches the caster's alignment: lawful (good or neutral) find definitive shapes (a ruler, an abacus); chaotic find playful ones (whistles, small toys, a child's ball or jacks); neutral have it easiest — an item associated with their class or specialty serves (a twig shaped like a wand for a generalist; a lodestone or divining rod for a diviner).
elysium.power_keys: Shaped by the granting power's portfolio: miniature rakes or scythes from agriculture gods, tiny tridents or veil-worn nets from sea powers, ankhs from desert powers, arms and armor from war gods — some usable in battle as blessed items (the bearer enjoys a bless effect while carrying a functioning key and keeping the power's favor).

carceri.spell_keys: Common items any berk could scavenge — but requirements change WITHOUT WARNING, so no list stays reliable. Last known: alteration — a lead necklace worn wrapped around the caster's wrist; conjuration/summoning — a perfectly round, fist-sized lodestone; divination — a good quantity of the caster's OWN blood (the alternative to sacrificing a comrade); necromancy — the thigh bone of a farastu gehreleth.
carceri.power_keys: Seldom granted: the powers here read reliance on keys as weakness, preferring priests who survive on wit and strength (a few contrary powers grant on a whim). Keys are prominent portfolio items — Malar's might be animal claws or fangs, Raiden's arrows or drums.

gehenna.spell_keys: School-focused and pattern-learnable (decent intuition can guess them): currently the necromancy key is the skull of someone slain in anger, Elemental Fire's a hunk of still-warm obsidian. Keys drift continuously — within a year the set is almost entirely different (last year's necromancy key was a yagnoloth fingerbone; next year's might be prime graveyard dirt) — but an expired key keeps working about three years.
gehenna.power_keys: Friendly powers shun Gehenna and its evil residents seldom grant. Sung Chiang might key an especially deserving priest — after making him steal it first.

the-gray-waste.spell_keys: A different form on each layer — at least three keys per school, each with some affinity to it: charm person on Oinos wants a small mirror reflecting the light of the caster's own eyes; Pluton's necromancy key is said to be a stone plucked from a petitioner's mouth.
the-gray-waste.power_keys: Rarely granted (why sharpen an edge when all ends in gloom?) except to very favored servants — or to followers of pantheon allies: most keys restore a single sphere, the asking power's specialty (a Greek cleric might find his Healing sphere restored in Pluton because Hades stays on good terms with Olympus). Shape: the granting power's holy symbol marked with the sphere it carries.
